findings.problem: The solution requires combining like terms to turn x+(x+2)+(x+4) into 3x+6. This part never explains like terms or how to combine them. Part 3 teaches the method, but this part gives no reference to it.
findings.source: Content checklist L25–L26; [OpenStax Prealgebra 2e, §2.2: Simplify Expressions by Combining Like Terms](https://openstax.org/books/prealgebra-2e/pages/2-2-evaluate-simplify-and-translate-expressions).

findings.quote: An **exponent** tells how many times a number or variable is used as a factor.
findings.problem: This definition requires a positive integer exponent, but the lesson states no restriction. Negative exponents do not count repeated factors. For example, 2^(-1)=1/2, which cannot mean using 2 as a factor negative one times.
findings.source: Content checklist B01; [OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, §6.7: Use the Definition of a Negative Exponent](https://openstax.org/books/elementary-algebra-2e/pages/6-7-integer-exponents-and-scientific-notation).
